39768-vassall-morton-a-novel.creator: Unknown

He looks with as much awe at Harvard College library as I did myself forty-five years ago, when I came down from Steuben to join the freshman class."

7998-the-frogs.title: The Frogs
7998-the-frogs.creator: Aristophanes
7998-the-frogs.description: A book by Aristophanes. as elsewhere, he stands for tradition against innovation of all kinds, whether in politics, religion, or art. The hostility to Euripides displayed here and in several other plays, like his attacks on Socrates, is a result of this attitude of conservatism. The present play is notable also as a piece of elaborate if not over-serious literary criticism from the pen of a great poet._

arxiv-1711-02924.title: Out-of-equilibrium chiral and U A ​ ( 1 ) U_{A}(1) symmetry breaking in electromagnetic fields
arxiv-1711-02924.creator: Xingyu Guo and Pengfei Zhuang
arxiv-1711-02924.description: Abstract We systematically study quantum effect on chiral and U A ​ ( 1 ) U_{A}(1) symmetry breaking under external electromagnetic fields in the frame of equal-time Wigner function formalism. We derive the transport and constraint equations for the quark distribution functions and the chiral and pion condensates in a Nambu–Jona-Lasinio model.

arxiv-2108-05670.title: Communication Optimization in Large Scale Federated Learning using Autoencoder Compressed Weight Updates
arxiv-2108-05670.creator: Srikanth Chandar, Pravin Chandran, Raghavendra Bhat, Avinash Chakravarthi
arxiv-2108-05670.description: Abstract Federated Learning (FL) solves many of this decade’s concerns regarding data privacy and computation challenges. FL ensures no data leaves its source as the model is trained at where the data resides. However, FL comes with its own set of challenges. The communication of model weight updates in this distributed environment comes with significant network bandwidth costs.

arxiv-2205-13697.title: FedFormer: Contextual Federation with Attention in Reinforcement Learning Conference: Proc. of the 22nd International Conference on Autonomous Agents and Multiagent Systems (AAMAS 2023); May 29 – June 2, 2023; London, United Kingdom 316
arxiv-2205-13697.creator: Liam Hebert, Lukasz Golab, Pascal Poupart, Robin Cohen
arxiv-2205-13697.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Liam Hebert, Lukasz Golab, Pascal Poupart, Robin Cohen. A core issue in multi-agent federated reinforcement learning is defining how to aggregate insights from multiple agents. This is commonly done by taking the average of each participating agent’s model weights into one common model (FedAvg). We instead propose FedFormer, a novel federation strategy that utilizes Transformer Attention to contextually aggregate embeddings from models originating from different learner agents.

arxiv-2208-13245.title: Continuous-time balanced truncation for time-periodic fluid flows using frequential Gramians
arxiv-2208-13245.creator: Alberto Padovan, Clarence W. Rowley
arxiv-2208-13245.description: Abstract Reduced-order models for flows that exhibit time-periodic behavior (e.g., flows in turbomachinery and wake flows) are critical for several tasks, including active control and optimization. One well-known procedure to obtain the desired reduced-order model in the proximity of a periodic solution of the governing equations is continuous-time balanced truncation.

arxiv-2306-05094.title: On the Robustness of Topics API to a Re-Identification Attack Volume: YYYY X DOI: XXXXXXX.XXXXXXX
arxiv-2306-05094.creator: Nikhil Jha, Martino Trevisan, Emilio Leonardi, Marco Mellia
arxiv-2306-05094.description: Abstract . Web tracking through third-party cookies is considered a threat to users’ privacy and is supposed to be abandoned in the near future. Recently, Google proposed the Topics API framework as a privacy-friendly alternative for behavioural advertising. Using this approach, the browser builds a user profile based on navigation history, which advertisers can access.

arxiv-2312-04379.title: How much informative is your XAI? A decision-making assessment task to objectively measure the goodness of explanations
arxiv-2312-04379.creator: Marco Matarese, Francesco Rea, Alessandra Sciutti
arxiv-2312-04379.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Marco Matarese, Francesco Rea, Alessandra Sciutti. There is an increasing consensus about the effectiveness of user-centred approaches in the explainable artificial intelligence (XAI) field. Indeed, the number and complexity of personalised and user-centred approaches to XAI have rapidly grown in recent years. Often, these works have a two-fold objective: (1) proposing novel XAI techniques able to consider the users and (2) assessing the goodness of such techniques with respect to others.

arxiv-2503-20566.title: Accurate Gauge-Invariant Tensor Network Simulations for Abelian Lattice Gauge Theory in (2+1)D: ground state and real-time dynamics
arxiv-2503-20566.creator: Yantao Wu, Wen-Yuan Liu
arxiv-2503-20566.description: Abstract We propose a novel tensor network method to achieve accurate and efficient simulations of Abelian lattice gauge theories (LGTs) in (2+1)D for both ground state and real-time dynamics. The first key is to identify a gauge canonical form (GCF) of gauge-invariant tensor network states, which already simplifies existing algorithms for (1+1)D LGTs.

arxiv-2508-10449.title: SkeySpot: Automating Service Key Detection for Digital Electrical Layout Plans in the Construction Industry
arxiv-2508-10449.creator: Dhruv Dosi, Rohit Meena, Param Rajpura, Yogesh Kumar Meena
arxiv-2508-10449.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Dhruv Dosi, Rohit Meena, Param Rajpura, Yogesh Kumar Meena. Legacy floor plans, often preserved only as scanned documents, remain essential resources for architecture, urban planning, and facility management in the construction industry. However, the lack of machine-readable floor plans render large-scale interpretation both time-consuming and error-prone. Automated symbol spotting offers a scalable solution by enabling the identification of service key symbols directly from floor plans, supporting workflows such as cost estimation, infrastructure maintenance, and regulatory compliance.

arxiv-2509-22870.title: Lexicon-Enriched Graph Modeling for Arabic Document Readability Prediction
arxiv-2509-22870.creator: Passant Elchafei, Mayar Osama, Mohamed Rageh, Mervat Abuelkheir
arxiv-2509-22870.description: Abstract We present a graph-based approach enriched with lexicons to predict document-level readability in Arabic, developed as part of the Constrained Track of the BAREC Shared Task 2025. Our system models each document as a sentence-level graph, where nodes represent sentences and lemmas, and edges capture linguistic relationships such as lexical co-occurrence and class membership.

arxiv-2510-26942.title: Harnessing Floquet dynamics for selective metrology in few-qubit systems
arxiv-2510-26942.creator: Asghar Ullah, Hasan Mermer, Melih Özkurt, Igor Lesanovsky, Özgür E. Müstecaplıoğlu
arxiv-2510-26942.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Asghar Ullah, Hasan Mermer, Melih Özkurt, Igor Lesanovsky, Özgür E. Müstecaplıoğlu. Periodically driven quantum systems can function as highly selective parameter filters. We demonstrate this capability in a finite-size, three-qubit system described by the transverse-field Floquet Ising model. In this system, we identify a period-doubling (PD) dynamical phase that exhibits a stark asymmetry in metrological sensitivity to the magnetic field applied on the qubits and to the coupling strength between the qubits.

pmc-11477460.creator: Abd Wahab Amer Taufek, Yaacob Najib Majdi, Mohd Hairon Suhaily, Abdul Aziz Zariah
pmc-11477460.description: BackgroundStroke ranks as the second leading cause of death globally, contributing to 15.2 million deaths in 2016. In Malaysia, stroke has emerged as a significant cause of mortality and disability. This study aims to evaluate the survival time and rate of stroke patients in Malaysia.

pmc-12592951.title: Early Vasopressin in Septic Shock—Promise, Paradox, and the Pursuit of Precision
pmc-12592951.creator: Jay Prakash, Khushboo Saran, Bodhisatwa Choudhuri
pmc-12592951.description:
A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). How to cite this article: Prakash J, Saran K, Choudhuri B. Early Vasopressin in Septic Shock—Promise, Paradox, and the Pursuit of Precision. Indian J Crit Care Med 2025;29(10):799–801.Keywords: Early intervention, Hemodynamic optimization, Septic shock, Vasopressin

Septic shock remains one of the most challenging issues in critical care medicine—a state of circulatory collapse driven not by a single insult but by a complex interplay of infection, inflammation, and dysregulated host response.

pmc-12717994.title: Genome Variation in Three Anthophora Bee Species Reflects Divergent Demographic Histories
pmc-12717994.creator: Demetris Taliadoros, André E R Soares, Guilherme Dias, Ignas Bunikis, Martin Pippel, Anna Olsson, Mai‐Britt Mosbech, Julia Heintz, Nina Lager, Anna‐Sofi Strand, Mats Pettersson, Olga Vinnere Pettersson, Henrik Lantz, Björn Cederberg, Kerstin Lindblad‐Toh, Matthew T Webster
pmc-12717994.description: Population genomics can reveal trends and drivers of biodiversity loss, but it is still unclear how best to use measures of genome variation to understand population vulnerability in insects. Here we study genome variation in three species of Anthophora bees that show contrasting population trends in northern Europe.

pmc-12729775.title: Pig Health Assessment Framework Based on Behavioural Analysis
pmc-12729775.creator: Shuqin Tu, Boyang Tan, Aqing Yang, Hairan Yang, Yizhi Luo, Yuan Fang, Zicong Xu, Danilo Florentino Pereira
pmc-12729775.description: Simple SummaryThis study proposes a pig health assessment framework based on multi-object tracking (MOT), which automatically tracks and quantifies pig behaviour in large-scale pig farming. The framework consists of an MOT module, a behaviour statistics and analysis module, and a health assessment module.

pmc-13180931.title: Design, development, and validation of a multimodal synergy-based intuitive virtual and augmented reality therapy platform for mental health
pmc-13180931.creator: Parthan Olikkal, Oritsejolomisan Mebaghanje, Viraj Janeja, Sruthi Sundharram, Golnaz Moharrer, Akshara Ajendla, Andrea Kleinsmith, Ann Sofie Clemmensen, Rajasekhar Anguluri, Adam Culbreth, Ramana Vinjamuri
pmc-13180931.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Embodied therapies such as movement therapy have shown promise in enhancing emotional regulation, cognitive engagement, and physical rehabilitation. However, scalable and personalized delivery of such interventions remains a critical challenge. This work presents SIVAM (Synergy-based Intuitive Virtual and Augmented Mental Health platform), a multimodal system that integrates immersive virtual environments, markerless motion capture, physiological sensing, and humanoid robotic mirroring to support affect-aware interventions for mental health.

pmc-13355593.title: Automated high-resolution CT analysis outperforms visual assessment in predicting interstitial lung disease progression in SSc
pmc-13355593.creator: Francesca Motta, Antonio Tonutti, Federica Catapano, Gianluca Sellaro, Francesco Amati, Anna Stainer, Calogero Messana, Stefano Aliberti, Marco Francone, Carlo Selmi, Maria De Santis
pmc-13355593.description: ObjectivesProgressive interstitial lung disease (ILD) is the leading cause of mortality in SSc. Early recognition of progression is crucial to timely treatment, but reliable early markers are lacking. Automated quantitative analysis of chest high-resolution CT (HRCT) may provide an objective tool to detect early progression.

pmc-13648057.title: A trial emulation study indirectly comparing tafamidis and acoramidis in transthyretin amyloid cardiomyopathy: the ReplicATTR study
pmc-13648057.creator: Philippe Debonnaire, Peter-Paul Zwetsloot, Roman Pfister, Pau Llàcer, Alberto Cipriani, Paolo Milani, Diana Bonderman, Christoph Ohlmeier, Thomas Evers, Richard Wyss, Elisabetta Patorno, Riddhi Doshi, Julien Beisel, Craig I Coleman, Carlos Aguiar, Tomas Ripoll-Vera
pmc-13648057.description: Aim:Tafamidis and acoramidis are transthyretin stabilizers approved for the treatment of transthyretin amyloid cardiomyopathy. We compared the effectiveness of acoramidis versus tafamidis regarding all-cause mortality (ACM).Materials & methods:This study used a hybrid design to compare 42-month ACM with acoramidis versus tafamidis using trial emulation, calibration, and indirect treatment comparison.

pmc-13668396.title: Artificial Intelligence–Driven Norepinephrine Control Using Adaptive Cardiac Digital Twin for Critical Care Patients
pmc-13668396.creator: Vidya S. Nair, G. D. Heshan Niranga, Thushara Madathil, Rahul Krishnan Pathinarupothi
pmc-13668396.description: BackgroundInfusion pumps are used in critical care settings to deliver medicines such as norepinephrine (NE), insulin, and certain nutrients. Currently, clinicians preset the infusion rate in the device, usually for 1 hour, resulting in a constant drug delivery. However, a patient's response to a preset infusion can vary over time depending on their vital changes.
